The backend handling for /proc/net/if_inet6 in addrconf.c doesn't properly
handle starting/stopping the iteration.  The problem is that at some point
during the iteration
column2: an overflow is detected and the process is

column1: subsequently stopped.  The item being shown via seq_printf() when the
overflow occurs is not actually shown
subsequently called to resume iterating
thus the item that was being processed when the overflow occurred never
gets printed.
Alter the meaning of the private data member ""offset"".  Currently
is not 0 (which only happens at the very beginning)
the next hlist item to be printed.  After this change
represents the current item.
This is also consistent with the private data member ""bucket""
represents the current bucket
column2: and also the use of ""pos"" as defined in

column1: seq_file.txt:
The pos passed to start() will always be either zero
recent pos used in the previous session.
